doc.title: J. Leo Rayhill interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 23, 2007

title: Race relations in Utica and Joe Sullivan at Tommy Joy's
summary: Relations were good; he heard Joe Sullivan and Art Hodes nightly at Tommy Joy's.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Let me take you back. We’re going to talk about your show a little more, but I’m curious about Utica in the 1940s and sort of this jazz club scene in your high school. What was the racial relations like back then?
It was pretty good. Because they had, I remember being in Tommy Joy’s a number of times, I practically lived there with Joe Sullivan. Remember Joe Sullivan?
